how.title: From idea to secret match in 4 steps

s1.title: Create in 60 seconds
s1.body: Pick a service, name it, set a date and a budget. Our wizard guides you.

s2.title: Invite your people
s2.body: Paste a list of emails. Everyone gets a festive invite and joins with one code.

s3.title: Fair, smart draw
s3.body: One click. Nobody gets themselves, and couples or last year's pairs stay apart.

s4.title: The big reveal
s4.body: Each person flips their card to see who they gift, plus that person's wishlist.

examples.title: Made for every kind of group

office.name: Acme Holiday Swap
office.rule: Managers never draw their own team
office.story: HR set it up during a coffee break, pasted the team list from a spreadsheet and ran the draw on Friday. Everyone found their match by Monday, with wishlists, and nobody had to pull names from a hat over Zoom.

family.name: Gómez Family Christmas
family.story: Abuela's house, three households, two time zones. Each cousin wrote a wishlist, couples were kept apart automatically, and the reveal happened on everyone's phone at dinner.

books.name: Midnight Readers
books.story: The club runs a book swap every December. QuickSanta remembers who read what, keeps last year's pairs apart, and everyone shares a 'books I love' wishlist.

pricing.title: Free for friends. Powerful for teams.

pro.name: Pro
features: All services: Wishlist Exchange, Book & Cookie swaps

faq.title: Questions?
faq.a1: Yes. Exchanges with up to 20 people are free. For bigger groups (up to 100 people), Pro is $8.90 per month per workspace and you can cancel anytime.
faq.q2: Can the organizer see who got whom?
faq.a2: No. Matches are private: only each participant sees their own. Organizers just see who has revealed.
faq.q3: Do people need a password or an app?
faq.a3: No. Everyone signs in with a 6-digit code sent to their email, on any phone or computer.
faq.a4: Yes. Add rules like 'Ana and Bruno never draw each other' and the draw always respects them.

final.title: Ready to make this year's exchange the easiest ever?
